## Summary

- **18/18 high (>=0.70)**, 0 uncertain, 0 fallback
- D9 ship gate: >=80% at >=0.70 -> needed 15/18, actual 18/18, **PASS**

## Observations worth discussing in D9

1. **The 0.70 gate is trivially met.** 18/18 cleared it.
2. **`size_outlier` shows up on 10/18 books** — likely the parser is merging table-of-contents / preface into chapter 1, producing one >>>5x-average section. Worth investigating whether the front-matter merging is intentional or a bug.
3. **`single_section` only fires on Modest Proposal** (correctly — it's one essay).
4. **Scores bunch at 0.79 or 1.00.** No book lands in the 0.80-0.99 band. The penalty table is coarse-grained — every book either has `size_outlier` (drops to 0.79) or doesn't (stays at 1.00).
5. **5 "expected low" predictions all scored "high"** — my band predictions were off. The parser handles named chapters / roman numerals / numbered books better than I expected. Books I predicted as hard (Walden, Meditations, Republic) actually have detectable structure that the heuristic finds.

## Concerns to weigh before shipping

- **Under-detection is invisible.** The Republic shows 4 sections; the actual book has 10 numbered Books. The heuristic gave it 1.00 confidence and the user would never see a badge. If under-detection is common, the badge is too quiet.
- **The 0.79 cluster.** Every book with size_outlier lands at exactly the same score. That suggests the penalty is binary in practice. Worth considering whether to keep the penalty or replace with a more graduated signal.

## What this calibration does NOT measure

- Chapter detection **accuracy** — only whether the heuristic was suspicious enough to flag.
- Per-chapter title quality.
- Reader experience after override editing.
